purpose: silver_flights holds one cleaned record per scheduled flight leg departing a NYC-area airport (EWR, JFK, or LGA) during the profiled period (2013-01-01 through 2013-06-30), combining flight schedule and performance facts with carrier, aircraft, and origin/destination airport reference attributes.
usage: Read the table at the grain of flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport; join on these keys to get one row per scheduled flight leg. Consumers must handle nulls in dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes for flights that were cancelled or diverted (cross-check is_cancelled), and nulls in tail_number and the aircraft_* and dest_* reference columns where no match was found in the underlying reference data.
limitations: The declared grain of flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, origin_airport is inferred from a table-wide duplicate_row_rate of 0.0 plus column cardinalities; it is not yet confirmed by a deterministic grain measurement. Aircraft reference attributes (manufacturer, model, manufacture_year, seat_count, engine_type) are null for roughly 16-18% of rows and destination reference attributes (airport_name, municipality, iso_region, elevation_ft, longest_runway_ft) are null for roughly 2.1% of rows where no reference match was found. Delay and actual-time columns are null for roughly 3% of rows, likely cancelled or diverted flights. captured_at resembles an ingestion timestamp but is not flagged as airbyte metadata in the profile; its treatment as a regular column should be re-checked by the reviewer.
